Walmart announces it will officially begin supporting Apple Pay next week. The retailer resisted offering Apple Pay for over a decade, despite continued consumer pressure.

Apple Pay 終於登陸 Walmart

Walmart announced the news in a press release today. Starting August 24, the company will roll out contactless payment options, including Apple Pay, at select Walmart and Sam's Club locations. The feature will reach all U.S. stores by the end of this year and extend to gas stations by mid-2027.

Walmart is broadly adding support for contactless payments, including Apple Pay, Google Pay, contactless credit cards, and other payment platforms on iPhone and Apple Watch. Customers will also be able to add their Walmart and Sam's Club membership cards to Apple Wallet and other platforms. Contactless payment will operate alongside existing payment methods, including Walmart's own Walmart Pay.

The company says:

Walmart is one of the last major retailers that still did not support Apple Pay, making this big news for consumers. For years, the retailer refused to offer contactless payment, insisting on its QR code-based payment system, Walmart Pay.

Until last year, Walmart was doubling down on its belief that Walmart Pay offered a more convenient experience for customers than Apple Pay. However, to use Walmart Pay, users had to first link a debit or credit card in the Walmart app on iPhone, then scan a QR code at checkout to complete the purchase with iPhone.

A quick search on social media shows just how frustrated users have been with Walmart's refusal to support Apple Pay.

After all, most other longtime Apple Pay holdouts have caved in years ago, including Kroger, Home Depot, and H-E-B, and for good reason.

Did Walmart's lack of Apple Pay support ever affect your shopping habits? Will you be more inclined to visit Walmart and Sam's Club now that they offer Apple Pay? Let us know in the comments.
